source.title: On the Effects of Data Scale on UI Control Agents
source.authors: Wei Li; William E. Bishop; Alice Li; Christopher Rawles; Folawiyo Campbell-Ajala; Divya Tyamagundlu; O. Riva

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether downstream task performance changes predictably with training-data scale, using UI-agent step accuracy rather than held-out language-model loss.
record.gate_note: The study scales the amount of fine-tuning data for UI control agents and reports step accuracy, so it bears on V6. It does not test language-model loss scaling, parameter/token/compute laws, compute-optimal allocation, architecture shape, or the same power-law form in other modalities. Zero-shot and few-shot comparisons are not findings about the fine-tuned data-scale curve.
record.test_reason: The study tests V6 in a new setting by varying UI-agent fine-tuning demonstration counts and measuring downstream step accuracy, including accuracy-versus-log-data fits. It does not test pretraining loss laws or validate extrapolations on larger runs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors infer that more fine-tuning demonstrations may yield robust IDD performance, while slower OOD scaling makes robust high-level OOD performance potentially impractical through fine-tuning alone. These feasibility claims rely on extrapolations from one fine-tuned model, not demonstrated performance at the projected data sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA fine-tuning of PaLM 2S and UI action step accuracy while varying demonstration count; it does not use the original scaling-law loss measurement or model/data/compute allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Observed outcomes vary by instruction level, in-domain versus out-of-domain split, and LoRA rank. The paper reports wider IDD–OOD gaps at larger fine-tuning data scales, especially for high-level instructions and rank 64.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2024 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
record.problems: Only PaLM-2S was fine-tuned. The authors note offline evaluation does not reward alternative successful routes or corrective actions; projections to very large demonstration counts are extrapolations. No error bars or confidence intervals are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 zero-shot and few-shot methods are not fine-tuned data-scale points. Table 5 results for LT-5, LT-10, LT-100, LT-1k, and LT-1k-r64 were omitted to stay within the row limit; selected larger-scale results and all four test-split conditions are included.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Empirical validation of small-run loss predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger; the paper's accuracy projections are unvalidated extrapolations.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling exponents.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count and its effect on loss.
Whether a power-law functional form holds beyond text pretraining; accuracy linear in log demonstration count does not establish this.
Performance versus pretraining loss, pretraining model/token/compute scaling, other fine-tuned model families, and online task completion as data scales.
Dependence of power-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices; LoRA-rank accuracy differences alone do not test these.

missing.what: Few-shot demonstration-count sweep: Gemini 1.5 Pro HL accuracy 41.8%, 40.2%, 39.5%, and LL accuracy 50.2%, 50.8%, 53.3% at 5, 10, 100 demonstration equivalents. These are context-scale results relevant to V6, although distinct from fine-tuning.

Application-type data sweeps: rank-4 LT-5 through LT-10k HL accuracy rises from 38.8% to 74.8% on Google apps and 26.2% to 54.7% on third-party apps; LL rises from 57.5% to 79.2% and 56.3% to 77.9%. Record intermediate points and the separately ranked all-data endpoint.

Projected demonstration requirements: Section 4.4 estimates 500k LL and 1M HL episodes for 95% IDD step accuracy, and 2M for 99% HL step accuracy; Section 4.5 estimates 10M LL, 60M HL, and 150M HL respectively OOD. Mark these as unvalidated projections, not observed scale points. The conclusion inconsistently gives 1M for IDD LL.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. OOD accuracy below IDD does not by itself limit V6; the relevant qualification is the slower scaling trend and local reversals. Figure 5 changes LoRA rank with data quantity, and no uncertainty is reported. Table 5's omitted small-data rows are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run held-out loss from smaller runs.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices on loss.
Whether the same power-law form applies across modalities or training regimes; fine-tuning data is varied, but neither held-out loss nor the claimed loss-law form is measured.
Tests UI-agent step accuracy against fine-tuning data quantity, not a broad range of downstream tasks or performance against pretraining loss.
Does not test dependence of language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices.
